statement: From a given circle to cut off a segment admitting an angle equal to a given rectilineal angle.
heath_proof: Let ABC be the given circle, and the angle at D the given rectilineal angle; thus it is required to cut off from the circle ABC a segment admitting an angle equal to the given rectilineal angle, the angle at D. Let EF be drawn touching ABC at the point B, and on the straight line FB, and at the point B on it, let the angle FBC be constructed equal to the angle at D. [I. 23] Then, since a straight line EF touches the circle ABC, and BC has been drawn across from the point of contact at B, the angle FBC is equal to the angle constructed in the alternate segment BAC. [III. 32] But the angle FBC is equal to the angle at D; therefore the angle in the segment BAC is equal to the angle at D.  Therefore from the given circle ABC the segment BAC. has been cut off admitting an angle equal to the given rectilineal angle, the angle at D.

3.34
**Statement:** From a given circle to cut off a segment admitting an angle equal to a given rectilineal angle.

**Step 1.** Let ABC be the given circle and D the given rectilineal angle. It is required to cut off from the circle ABC a segment admitting an angle equal to the angle D.

**Step 2.** Let a straight line EF be drawn touching the circle ABC, and let B be the point of contact, so that EF touches the circle ABC at the point B [3.17].

**Step 3.** On the straight line FB, and at the point B on it, construct the angle FBC equal to the given angle D [1.23], the side BC being drawn on that side of EF on which the circle ABC lies.

**Step 4.** Since EF touches the circle ABC at B, no straight line can be interposed into the space between EF and the circumference of the circle [3.16]. Hence BC, being a straight line through B distinct from EF and lying on the side of the circle, falls within the circle; therefore, being produced, it meets the circumference again. Let C be the point at which it meets the circumference. Thus BC has been drawn across in the circle from the point of contact B and cuts the circle, and it cuts off from the circle the segment BAC lying on the opposite side of BC from F.

**Step 5.** Since the straight line EF touches the circle ABC at B, and from the point of contact B the straight line BC has been drawn across in the circle cutting it, the angle FBC which BC makes with the tangent is equal to the angle in the alternate segment BAC [3.32]; that is, to the angle BAC contained by the straight lines joined to B and C from any point A taken on the circumference of the segment BAC [D3.8].

**Step 6.** But the angle FBC was constructed equal to the angle D (Step 3). Therefore the angle in the segment BAC is also equal to the angle D [CN1].

**Step 7.** Therefore from the given circle ABC the segment BAC has been cut off admitting an angle equal to the given rectilineal angle D. Q.E.F.
